title: Work Begins On Ipswich’s Unitarian Meeting House

seo.title: Work Begins On Ipswich’s Unitarian Meeting House
seo.description: One of the oldest chapels in the country is to undergo a £550,000 restoration, with help from Historic England covering most of the cost.

heading: Work Begins On Ipswich’s Unitarian Meeting House
bodyHtml:
One of the oldest chapels in the country is to undergo a £550,000 restoration, with help from Historic England covering most of the cost, according to the Ipswich Star.

The 18th century Unitarian Meeting House, certainly one of Ipswich’s most significant buildings, has been a place of worship for 320 years, since opening its doors in 1700. The current congregation will be moving to a nearby community centre for the next seven months while the building is restored, updated, and given increased usability for more events.

On the day work began on the restoration, Historic England confirmed it would be making a grant for £421,000 for the work. The church had already raised £20,000 of its own, as well as been awarded further grants, boosting the funds to £125,000.

The rising Dissenter population in Ipswich in the 18th century gave cause for the church to be founded, and is now a Grade 1 listed building, along with its neighbour, the Willis headquarters.

Historic England has been heavily involved in the development of the plans for the project, giving expert fundraising advice, and technical guidance.

The Unitarian Meeting House had been placed on the Heritage at Risk Register due to the poor condition of the building, from which it will be removed once repairs are completed.

Tony Calladine, regional director at Historic England in the East of England said: “We’re pleased to play our part in repairing this important building and protecting it for future generations to enjoy. It will be a wonderful achievement to see it removed from the Heritage at Risk Register.”
